title: Fit the CSF-14 wave generator into a robot joint's mounted flexspline
instruction: Fit the wave generator into the gear until it is fully home, then let go.
context: Robot-joint assembly technicians fit wave generators to mounted spline pairs when building strain-wave joints. HDS Report 2025 describes five to six reducers per compact or collaborative robot; it does not count CSF-14 sets or manual insertions. This task isolates that fitting step on a CSF-14-50-2A-R: the maker requires rotation during insertion to avoid eccentric mesh and early failure. Motor coupling, cover fitting and powered joint testing follow outside this task.
setup: Millimetres; positions from the midpoint between the two arm bases (x forward, y to the robot's left), heights above the bench. Robot-joint assembly bench. A Harmonic Drive CSF-14-50-2A-R component set (0.09 kg, catalogue) in a printed PETG joint housing (72 across; supplied drawing lacks functional bearing seat and circular-spline bolt support; output flange unspecified) standing output side down in the 4 mm locating pocket of a black printed PLA assembly cradle (120 x 120 x 10), axis at x 290, y -90 (1.6 kg with the gear, estimate): the dark steel circular spline (50 pilot, 8 x M3 on a 44 circle) is bolted flush with the housing's top face 60 up; the bright flexspline cup (28.5 deep, round bore 31.0 before the generator goes in, 1.0 lead-in at its rim; estimates) stands open end up, level with that face, bolted to the output flange on a 6805-2RS bearing. The wave generator (17.6 tall: 30.4 steel plug 8.0 tall with a 1.2 chamfer and a red index mark, 23 black Oldham disc, 16 steel hub with a 6 bore; 30 g; plug and hub sizes estimated) stands plug down on the 4 floor of an aluminium parts tray (140 x 100 x 15). Lot A: tray centre x 195, y -225. Lot B: tray at x 385, y -215, generator turned 90 degrees. At the back (fixed): the joint's NEMA 17 stepper (42 x 42 x 48) on a printed 60 x 60 x 8 adapter plate at x 540, y 20, and the printed joint cover (72 x 20) at x 540, y -90. Real trial only: use dedicated sacrificial standard-profile gripper pads in place of the shared pads; inspect for burrs and keep grease off grasp surfaces. Background motor stays disconnected. Measuring tools: a tared platform scale under the cradle; heights are then from the scale's top. Trials are run on lots A and B and averaged; the screenshot shows lot A.
scoring: Read from overhead and side video (30 fps), a tared platform scale under the cradle (display in the side camera's view), a depth gauge on the circular spline face, a small square, and after the trial a dial indicator on a 6 mm shaft in the hub. Score 0 for the whole trial if, at any moment: the scale reads over 30 N (simulation: the press on the plug on the gear axis, 0.25 s mean; benchmark overload threshold); a gripper enters the flexspline below the circular spline face (rim marks under a 10x loupe, side video); the generator falls over 10 mm with no gripper on it anywhere but inside the gear; or the housing moves over 5 mm, or tilts or turns over 5 degrees (tape marks). Score 0 at the end if the mesh is eccentric (dedoidal): turning the hub slowly by hand through two turns, the shaft runs out over 0.3 mm on the dial indicator. In simulation the eccentric mesh is set by pushing the plug, on the gear axis, at 20 N for 0.25 s while it turns under 0.3 rad/s, or at 8 N while tilted over 3 degrees, and cleared only by lifting the plug out of the rim. Otherwise, with the generator's axis within 1 mm of the gear's and tilt at most 30 degrees: 1.0 home (hub top 9.7 mm or less above the circular spline face; hub square within 3 degrees), even mesh, both grippers at least 20 mm from the generator, generator and housing moving no more than 1 mm for 1 s (also below 20 mm/s and 0.5 rad/s); 0.75 home and even but held, or not yet still; 0.5 the plug at least half way into the teeth zone (hub top 12.65 mm or less above the face); 0.25 at least 1 mm into it (hub top 15.1 mm or less); 0 otherwise, including a generator lying on the rim or lifted out. Trials on lots A and B are averaged. The simulation also requires the mesh front to reach each credited depth; it allows 0.5 mm plug-depth tolerance. Partial-score nominal hub heights are 15.1 and 12.65 mm; their tolerated limits are 15.6 and 13.15 mm. The 30 N overload, 20 N straight-push and 8 N tilted-push thresholds are benchmark estimates, not published bearing ratings. The 0.3 mm runout cutoff and diagnostic are unvalidated benchmark choices, not maker acceptance criteria.
run_limit: 2,400 steps (120 s at 20 Hz) per trial; two trials (lots A and B), averaged
reset_notes: Ready-made matched CSF-14 set; no per-trial casting, printing or curing. The supplied fixture drawing lacks a functional bearing seat and bolt support; flange unspecified. Complete and check the physical fixture before trials; fabrication is not a 2-3 minute operation. With a finished fixture, allow 5-10 minutes to fit dedicated pads, mount, inspect and enrol a ready-made specimen before its first trial; allow 2-3 minutes between undamaged trials (both planning estimates, unmeasured). Keep a reset kit of depth gauge, dial indicator/base, straight 6 mm shaft, square, loupe, scale, tape, lint-free wipes, specified lubricant and dedicated sacrificial standard-profile pads. Store the shared pads separately. Score the mesh first: turn the shaft slowly through two turns and record runout. Lift the generator out by its hub; reject fresh burrs, tooth damage, bearing roughness or looseness. Keep all three components as one matched set; replace a damaged set, not an unmatched individual part. Check sacrificial pads for cuts and grease; replace before reuse. Return housing/tray to tape marks and generator plug down, red index toward +y (A) or -x (B). Confirm free output rotation, zero the depth gauge at the circular-spline face and tare the scale. Splines stay mounted. If replacement/enrolment takes longer, record it; do not count it as a normal reset.
fidelity: Catalogue-scale CSF-14; unlisted sizes, masses and friction are estimates. Rigid round plug/cup replace the flexible mesh: a contact-loaded stop advances 4 mm/turn under at least 1.5 N to 8.4 mm. Straight 20 N or tilted 8 N presses set an eccentric flag; withdrawal clears it. Force/feed values, 30 N overload and the 0.3 mm runout diagnostic are unvalidated benchmark choices. Mesh torque and output rotation are omitted. Physical fixture incomplete; no physical trials reported.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (lots A and B 0 each; both ran to the 2,400-step limit without refusing; the right hand moved between the tray and the housing but the generator was never fitted); demo: 1.0 in each of lots A and B (turned home, released, still at about 29 s)
